protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Confirmed. In the tail ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter introduced by 9d804c54ce962408ae6418255a83a13924f7145d, listener.onDataRead and flowController.consumeBytes execute before buf.release without a finally. Either call can throw and strand the handler-owned pooled ByteBuf, allowing remote DATA frames to accumulate direct-memory leaks and cause OOME. CVE-2026-48043 is PUBLISHED and the Netty GHSA names this mechanism and patched versions.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: Confirmed. Targeted git log -S and git log -L identify 9d804c54ce962408ae6418255a83a13924f7145d as the first 4.2 commit that writes the vulnerable tail-handler sequence. It is a single-parent public-history object and is the smallest surviving public first-write, despite changing other decompression files in the same commit.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: Confirmed. Immediate parent edb55fd8e0a3bcbd85881e423464f585183d1284 lacks the tail ChannelInboundHandlerAdapter and instead releases the current decompressed buffer in an enclosing try/finally after listener and flow-controller calls.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: Confirmed. The 4.2 BIC has exactly one public parent and no finer public member chain to substitute. The later 4.1 port 34894ac73b02efefeacd9c0972780b32dc3de04f has the same tree and parent as public PR-head object 89810f4e9921f90fde528a0cfd399266a9739d89, but that equivalent 4.1 object does not decompose or predate the selected 4.2 first-write.
protocol_checks.affected_and_fixed_release_membership: Confirmed. Ancestry and tag-file inspection show the 4.2 BIC absent from netty-4.2.4.Final, present and vulnerable in netty-4.2.5.Final through netty-4.2.14.Final, and fixed in netty-4.2.15.Final. The equivalent 4.1 first-write is absent from netty-4.1.124.Final, present and vulnerable in netty-4.1.125.Final through netty-4.1.134.Final, and fixed in netty-4.1.135.Final. Thus the advisory's upper bounds and patched tags are verified, while its lower bounds are broader than the actual introductions as the primary states.
protocol_checks.direct_fix_or_verified_unpatched_state: Confirmed. 3d45a1e4e8eb99144f716e54be5ac57e525fa7ca on 4.2 and db6138b168699736a6463c367e12ad0a4c36a25e on 4.1 directly wrap the vulnerable listener/flow-controller sequence in try/finally and move buf.release into finally; the fixed tag files contain that exact repair.
protocol_checks.bic_only_ai_attribution: Confirmed. The BIC commit object names human author Norman Maurer, GitHub as committer, and only human Co-authored-by trailer yawkat; it contains no Generated-with, Copilot, Cursor, Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, GPT, or bot marker. Attribution is based only on this BIC object, so NOT_AI is supported.

findings: The primary record's mechanism, BIC, immediate parent, release membership, direct fixes, and BIC-only AI attribution independently reproduce from the advisory and clone.

The advisory ranges overstate the vulnerable lower bounds: the vulnerable rewrite first ships in 4.1.125.Final and 4.2.5.Final, not all releases below the patched versions; the primary already records this distinction and it does not change the NOT_AI verdict.
